questions.question: Q5(a). In any triangle, prove that [(b-c)/a]*cos(A/2) = sin((B-C)/2).
questions.solution: (b-c)/a = (sinB - sinC)/sinA = [2*cos((B+C)/2)*sin((B-C)/2)]/[2*sin(A/2)*cos(A/2)] = [2*sin(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2)]/[2*sin(A/2)*cos(A/2)] = sin((B-C)/2)/cos(A/2). Multiplying by cos(A/2) gives sin((B-C)/2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q5(a); book p187 = PDF p215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cos^2(A/2) = (1+cosA)/2, then the projection law finishes it: b*cosA + a*cosB = c.
questions.question: Q5(b). In any triangle, prove that b*cos^2(A/2) + a*cos^2(B/2) = (a+b+c)/2.
questions.solution: b*cos^2(A/2) + a*cos^2(B/2) = b*(1+cosA)/2 + a*(1+cosB)/2 = [(a+b) + (b*cosA + a*cosB)]/2. By the projection law b*cosA + a*cosB = c, so this equals (a+b+c)/2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q5(b); book p187 = PDF p215 (vision read; s written as (a+b+c)/2 in print)

questions.knowledgeNote: cosB - cosC = -2*cos(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2) and c - b = -4R*sin(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2): the sine factors cancel.
questions.question: Q5(c). In any triangle, prove that a*(cosB - cosC) = 2*(c-b)*cos^2(A/2).
questions.solution: Left: a*(cosB - cosC) = 2R*sinA*[-2*sin((B+C)/2)*sin((B-C)/2)] = 2R*2*sin(A/2)*cos(A/2)*[-2*cos(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2)] = -8R*sin(A/2)*cos^2(A/2)*sin((B-C)/2). Right: 2*(c-b)*cos^2(A/2) = 4R*(sinC - sinB)*cos^2(A/2) = 4R*2*cos((B+C)/2)*sin((C-B)/2)*cos^2(A/2) = 8R*sin(A/2)*[-sin((B-C)/2)]*cos^2(A/2). Both sides agree.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q5(c); book p187 = PDF p215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Each weighted term becomes (cosC - cosB)/2: the three differences telescope to zero.
questions.question: Q5(d). In any triangle, prove that [(b-c)/a]*cos^2(A/2) + [(c-a)/b]*cos^2(B/2) + [(a-b)/c]*cos^2(C/2) = 0.
questions.solution: From Q5(a), (b-c)/a = sin((B-C)/2)/cos(A/2), so the first term is sin((B-C)/2)*cos(A/2) = [sin((B-C+A)/2) + sin((B-C-A)/2)]/2 = [sin((pi-2C)/2) + sin((-(pi-2B))/2)]/2 = (cosC - cosB)/2. Cyclically the second is (cosA - cosC)/2 and the third is (cosB - cosA)/2. Adding: [(cosC - cosB) + (cosA - cosC) + (cosB - cosA)]/2 = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q5(d); book p187 = PDF p215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Halve with (1+cosA)/2, then use bc*cosA + ca*cosB + ab*cosC = (a^2+b^2+c^2)/2.
questions.question: Q5(e). In any triangle, prove that bc*cos^2(A/2) + ca*cos^2(B/2) + ab*cos^2(C/2) = s^2, where 2s = a+b+c.
questions.solution: The left side is [bc*(1+cosA) + ca*(1+cosB) + ab*(1+cosC)]/2 = [(ab+bc+ca) + (bc*cosA + ca*cosB + ab*cosC)]/2. Now bc*cosA = (b^2+c^2-a^2)/2 and cyclically, so the bracket sum is (a^2+b^2+c^2)/2. Hence the left side is [(ab+bc+ca) + (a^2+b^2+c^2)/2]/2 = (a+b+c)^2/4 = s^2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q5(e); book p187 = PDF p215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: tan^2(A/2) = (s-b)(s-c)/[s(s-a)]: multiply the three and one factor cancels.
questions.question: Q5(f). In any triangle, prove that tan^2(A/2)*tan^2(B/2)*tan^2(C/2) = [(s-a)/s]*[(s-b)/s]*[(s-c)/s], where 2s = a+b+c.
questions.solution: By the half-angle formula tan^2(A/2) = (s-b)(s-c)/[s(s-a)], and cyclically for B and C. Multiplying: numerator (s-b)(s-c)*(s-c)(s-a)*(s-a)(s-b) = [(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)]^2; denominator s^3*(s-a)(s-b)(s-c). Cancelling one factor (s-a)(s-b)(s-c) gives (s-a)(s-b)(s-c)/s^3 = [(s-a)/s]*[(s-b)/s]*[(s-c)/s].
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q5(f); book p187 = PDF p215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: cot(B/2) + cot(C/2) = sinA/[sin(B/2)*sin(C/2)]: half-angles are compulsory (full angles fail: test the 3-4-5 triangle).
questions.question: Q5(g). In any triangle, prove that (b+c-a)*[cot(B/2) + cot(C/2)] = 2a*cot(A/2).
questions.solution: cot(B/2) + cot(C/2) = sin((B+C)/2)/[sin(B/2)*sin(C/2)] = cos(A/2)/[sin(B/2)*sin(C/2)], so the left side is 2(s-a)*cos(A/2)/[sin(B/2)*sin(C/2)]. Now (s-a) = 4R*cos(A/2)*sin(B/2)*sin(C/2) (from r = 4R*sin(A/2)*sin(B/2)*sin(C/2) and tan(A/2) = r/(s-a)). Substituting: 2*4R*cos(A/2)*sin(B/2)*sin(C/2)*cos(A/2)/[sin(B/2)*sin(C/2)] = 8R*cos^2(A/2). The right side is 2a*cot(A/2) = 4R*sinA*cos(A/2)/sin(A/2) = 8R*cos^2(A/2). Both sides agree. (Check on 3-4-5 with A = 90 deg: left = 2*(cot(B/2)+cot(C/2)) = 2*(2.414+0.414) = 5.657 = 2*5*cot45.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q5(g); book p187 = PDF p215 (vision read; half-angles confirmed in print)

questions.knowledgeNote: a^2*cotA = R*a*(b^2+c^2-a^2)/(bc): summing gives R*(2*sum a^2b^2 - sum a^4)/(abc) = 4*Delta by Heron.
questions.question: Q13(a). In any triangle, prove that a^2*cotA + b^2*cotB + c^2*cotC = 4*Delta.
questions.solution: a^2*cotA = a^2*cosA/sinA = a^2*[(b^2+c^2-a^2)/(2bc)]/(a/2R) = R*a*(b^2+c^2-a^2)/(bc) = R*a^2*(b^2+c^2-a^2)/(abc). Summing cyclically gives R/(abc)*[sum a^2*(b^2+c^2-a^2)] = R/(abc)*[2*(a^2*b^2+b^2*c^2+c^2*a^2) - (a^4+b^4+c^4)]. By Heron's form 16*Delta^2 = 2*sum a^2b^2 - sum a^4, so this is R*16*Delta^2/(abc) = 16R*Delta^2/(4R*Delta) = 4*Delta (using abc = 4R*Delta).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q13(a); book p188 = PDF p215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Equality holds because a/sinA = 2R is constant: both sides equal 4R^2*(sum sin^2)^2.
questions.question: Q13(b). In any triangle, prove that (a*sinA + b*sinB + c*sinC)^2 = (a^2+b^2+c^2)*(sin^2A + sin^2B + sin^2C).
questions.solution: Since a = 2R*sinA (and cyclically), the left side is [2R*(sin^2A + sin^2B + sin^2C)]^2 = 4R^2*(sin^2A + sin^2B + sin^2C)^2. The right side is [4R^2*(sin^2A + sin^2B + sin^2C)]*(sin^2A + sin^2B + sin^2C), which is the same. (This is Cauchy-Schwarz with equality, because (a, b, c) is proportional to (sinA, sinB, sinC).)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q13(b); book p188 = PDF p215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: sinA + sinB + sinC = (a+b+c)/(2R) = s/R: just add the three sine-rule fractions.
questions.question: Q13(c). In any triangle, prove that sinA + sinB + sinC = s/R, where 2s = a+b+c.
questions.solution: sinA + sinB + sinC = a/(2R) + b/(2R) + c/(2R) = (a+b+c)/(2R) = 2s/(2R) = s/R.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q13(c); book p188 = PDF p215 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Expand a*cosB*cosC with a = y+z style substitution: sum = [sum a^2 - sum(b-c)^2 ... ]/(4R) = Delta/R.
questions.question: Q13(d). In any triangle, prove that a*cosB*cosC + b*cosC*cosA + c*cosA*cosB = Delta/R.
questions.solution: a*cosB*cosC = 2R*sinA*cosB*cosC, so the left side is 2R*[sinA*cosB*cosC + sinB*cosC*cosA + sinC*cosA*cosB]. Dividing the bracket by cosA*cosB*cosC gives tanA + tanB + tanC, which equals tanA*tanB*tanC (standard A+B+C = pi identity). Hence the bracket is cosA*cosB*cosC*tanA*tanB*tanC = sinA*sinB*sinC, and the sum is 2R*sinA*sinB*sinC = 2R*(abc/8R^3) = abc/(4R^2) = Delta/R (using abc = 4R*Delta).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.6 Ex 6.1 Q13(d); book p188 = PDF p215 (vision read)
